notes: Your screenshot showed the real blocker: "spotify is rate limiting this app — waiting 20s (3 so far)" with the counter still on zero. Obeying the delay was never going to be enough, because four workers went straight back to bursting and earned the next one. The Spotify client now PACES itself: after the first 429 it spaces its requests, doubles the gap on each further one, and eases it back after a long clean run so one bad patch does not slow a two-hour migration for ever. A run that is not being throttled is never paced at all, so Qobuz and smaller libraries are untouched. The arithmetic: 9,635 albums is one search plus up to two track-listing reads each, about 29,000 requests — paced just under the limit that is a couple of hours and it finishes, whereas bursting into a 20-second wait every few requests it never does. Combined with 0.3.1 writing matches as it makes them and misses being cached, a run that is interrupted now keeps its progress and the next one picks up where it left off.
